key_insight: An LLM coding agent can turn one real calibration episode into action-labelled, multiview robot training data that supports direct deployment on real hardware.
engineering_relevance: The approach reduces repeated robot and operator use, with reported costs of $107 per hour of three-view data versus quoted teleoperation costs of $117 in China and $290 in North American labour alone.
method: Given a data request and calibration episode, the agent builds a simulated scene, expert controller, and success judge.
Simulation supplies exact actions; a real-image-conditioned video model renders synchronized, consistent camera views.
Independent judges check the expert and each rendered episode before admitting data for policy training.
evidence_signal: Across five real-robot tasks, farm-trained policies achieved 93/100 successes versus 84/100 for teleoperation-trained policies; under an unseen tablecloth and coloured light, they achieved 87 versus 46.
watch_item: Evidence covers only five tasks; broader deployment requires validating rendering fidelity and automated judges on new scenes and robot behaviours.
paper_title: PyRUA-DataFarm: LLM Agent as a Cost-Efficient Teleoperator for Real-Ready Robot Data
